hook: SCP-3693 is a ceramic statue of a young woman that can only be seen with your eyes shut, and when you do see it, it glides right up to your face. The article is very short, and nearly everything unsettling is packed into a brief discovery note at the end. Its title marks it as a postscript, and the page credits it as a co-written piece by djkaktus and The Great Hippo.
whyItMatters:
It works by inversion: the anomaly is about looking, yet the statue only exists for you when you choose not to look, so the safe act and the frightening one are the same. The report stresses that it has never acted with hostility, and the whole piece leans on that calm.

Its tags file it alongside the wiki's other sculpture-themed articles. The postscript label in the title is worth keeping in mind as you read.
thingsToNotice:
The main body is almost gentle: a statue that hovers in close, matches your eye level, follows you while your eyes stay closed and freezes when you open them, leaving people with a sense of being watched and some mild unease. The weight lands in the addendum. In 1995 agents chasing a local legend on Hashima Island, about a woman murdered by a lover she had rejected, found it in a warehouse basement up against a glass partition, surrounded by crushed concrete, twisted rebar and floor drains clogged with blood and faeces, with a woman's body with a broken neck close by.

When they returned after removing the statue, the basement could not be found again, and the dead woman's identity is still being investigated. The article stops there and leaves both questions open.
